steps: Coordinator grants bounded ownership with epoch 7.
Healthy holder renews while using epoch 7 on every write.
Pause or partition prevents renewal, so authority expires.
Successor receives epoch 8 and resources reject any returning epoch 7 work.

production.scenario: Kafka Connect task ownership is renewed continuously so connector work can move safely when pods die or drain.
components: connector configs and source offsets arriving from many enterprise integrations
service boundary that assigns tasks and accepts worker heartbeats
control-plane service that grants time-bounded task authority to worker pods
durable authority in the internal config topic and metadata store for owner and expiry
run connector tasks only while their current lease remains valid
control path that revokes, reassigns, and drains ownership during deploys or failures
observability path for lease expiry, rebalance churn, and duplicate task risk
flows: Connector tasks need an owner before source reads or sink writes can begin.
The coordinator requests a time-bounded lease for one task and one worker pod.
The authoritative metadata store records the worker owner, generation, and expiry.
A worker starts processing only after it receives a current lease-backed assignment.
The rebalance manager forces lease turnover before deployment or after a dead worker is detected.
Expired or conflicting assignments are surfaced from durable metadata for reassignment.
Dashboards show renewals, forced revocations, and potential duplicate-run windows.
